title: Trim observability cold path: introduce lazy-instrumentation and pooled-metric-harvester
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: runtime service pods pay a significant cold-start and steady-state memory tax from eager observability initialization. OpenTelemetry SDKs, multiple metric registries, and log adapters allocate on process start; combined with high-cardinality label hooks this increases p95 cold-start by ~120ms and heap by ~60-120MB for small worker containers.

Goal: reduce observability startup cost and persistent heap while preserving signal fidelity for SLOs. Implement two parallel strategies: 1) lazy-instrumentation so only critical traces/metrics are activated on first use, and 2) a pooled, batched metric harvester (pooled-metric-harvester) to centralize metric aggregation and reduce label churn/allocations.

Out of scope: changing customer-facing sampling policies or removing any exporter integrations. This is an infra-side optimization intended to be transparent to API consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p95 for runtime worker reduced by >=30% on standard small container (512MB-2vCPU) in benchmark harness
Resident heap usage attributable to observability subsystems reduced by >=40MB across typical service images
No regression in end-to-end trace propagation for internal request flows (trace IDs preserved across RPC boundaries)
All unit and integration tests for observable instrumentation pass; new integration test for lazy-instrumentation coverage added
A rollout plan with gradual canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and rollback criteria documented in the PR and runbook
tasks: Prototype lazy-instrumentation wrapper around OpenTelemetry SDK initialization (language: Go) to defer heavy allocs until first instrumentation call
Implement pooled-metric-harvester with fixed-size worker pool to aggregate and compact label vectors before forwarding
Add environment flags: OBS_LAZY_INSTRUMENTATION=true and OBS_HARVESTER_POOL_SIZE= to allow toggling in staging
Benchmark harness runs: baseline, lazy-only, harvester-only, combined; record memory and p95 cold-start latency
Add integration tests that assert trace propagation and metric correctness under high-concurrency (500 rps burst)
Prepare rollout PR with feature gate and runtime-1.19 release notes entry
Coordinate with infra/helm to add config toggles for canary deployment and metrics retention impact monitoring
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed. Built a lightweight lazy-init shim that wraps otel SDK TracerProvider and MeterProvider. Initial microbenchmarks show lazy init eliminates ~90% of OTEL-related allocations on cold start when no traces are emitted.

2025-02-20: Design review with Observability team. Feedback: ensure trace context carrier initialization remains fast and add feature flag for gradual rollout. Agreed to keep default behavior unchanged until feature flag enabled at runtime.
2025-02-25: PR #4521 opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521). Implements lazy shim and simple pooled-harvester prototype. Requesting reviews from @sanjay, @linh, @ops-oncall.

2025-02-28: Benchmarks in staging harness (worker-small) against baseline: cold-start p95 reduced from 320ms -> 190ms (41% reduction) with lazy init only. Resident RSS dropped by ~58MB. Harvester prototype alone reduced steady-state alloc churn under 1k/s metric emplace bursts by 25%.

2025-03-03: Code review feedback addressed: added context sanitizer to avoid rare span leak on expedited shutdown; added metrics to track lazy-init occurrances and harvester queue length. New tests added for shutdown path.
2025-03-05: Integration tests running in CI/edge; staging canary scheduled for 2025-03-10 at 10% traffic. Post-canary verification checklist created and linked in PR description.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Lazy init could delay first trace emission for important startup spans. Mitigation: provide explicit API call init_observability() and default to warm init for control-plane processes
Risk: Harvester pool starvation under extreme concurrency. Mitigation: bounded backpressure + fallback synchronous drain path when queue saturates
Risk: Metric cardinality masking could obscure signals. Mitigation: harvester will only compact identical label vectors; label normalization logic reviewed with SRE
notes: Design decision: use lazy-init + feature flag rather than global OTEL SDK upgrade to keep change surface minimal
During spike we measured that third-party log adapters (fluent-connector) were responsible for ~30% of cold-start allocations — follow-up ticket suggested
If canary shows unexpected signal loss, we'll revert by disabling OBS_LAZY_INSTRUMENTATION and ramp down immediately
